content.title: Everything that happened on moving day at Augusta National
content.text: Young co-leads with McIlroy after 54 holesFollow live updates from the final round here.Rory McIlroy will go into the final round of the 2026 Masters with a share of the lead alongside Cameron Young at 11 under par.The defending champion squandered his record six-shot lead after yesterday’s second round by carding a 1-over 73. Young brilliantly reeled him with a 7-under 65 as the Players Championship winner hunts his first major championship.His 65 was tied with Scottie Scheffler for lowest round of the day as the two-time Masters champion finished at 7 under. He is one of nine players within five shots of the lead heading into Sunday's final round.Share your thoughts with us at live@theathletic.com. Want more Masters coverage? Sign up for our Golf Briefing newsletter here.WinnerPOSPLAYERTOTAL1Rory McIlroyNIR-12SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementYoung is unflappable and tied for the lead Getty ImagesWhy would a man who’s normally managing car seat triage, playing zone defense with three young kids, feel overwhelmed by a bad shot into the water? Why would a guy well-versed in the witching hours of dinner, bath and bedtime feel his heart rate rise standing over the water on Augusta National’s 15th hole with so much at stake?Cameron Young is a dad. Like, really a dad. He’s 28 years old with three kids under 5. He exhibits a stolid face under a polished yet matured beard that chooses not to emote. He’s somebody players ask for advice on their first kid, and their second, and definitely their third. Minutes after he won The Players Championship last month, he said he was still thinking about packing the family in the car and driving the four hours back to Jupiter, Fla. The dad energy radiated — let’s make good time.And Sunday morning, after loading the kids into the car, unloading them at Sunday mass, loading them up again, and then a final unload back at the rental house, he’ll head back to Augusta National to play 18 holes with a chance to win the Masters.How patrons tried to pick up McIlroy Getty ImagesA string of six pars. A cool and collected birdie on No. 10. It was a shaky front nine, but his scorecard looked a lot tidier than it actually was. Still, Rory McIlroy seemed to have caught a wave of momentum. That assessment couldn’t have been more wrong.I walked up to McIlroy’s group on No. 11 only to see him setting up for an approach shot some 50 yards behind Burns. It turned out, as a few patrons informed me, that McIlroy’s drive had hit the tree. So the next task appeared: Make a smooth swing, and don’t hit it in the water. We all know what McIlroy did next. A drop in the drop zone on the other side of the pond, a skillful chip and two putts. Suddenly, his historic six-shot lead was down to zero. He was tied with Cameron Young, and after a sloppy bogey on No. 12, he dropped to one shot behind the American.The patrons who packed onto the hill behind the 12th tee, with a view of that action on No. 11, winced in pain. But moments later, they were right back with the defending champion, rallying him on to a possible birdie. “That pit in my stomach has arrived, just 24 hours earlier than last year,” one patron told me. The rest of the round was the sort of emotional rollercoaster that has become standard practice for McIlroy followers, yet they still aren’t prepared every time it comes. On No. 13, McIlroy cleared an entire roped-off seating area for patrons (again!) only to punch out from the pine straw and hit a low, skinny wedge shot over the green. An unlikely birdie at No. 14 and a two-putt birdie on No. 15 once again kept the hope alive.McIlroy finished par, bogey, par to finish out his 73 and there was clear sentiment among the crowd at Augusta National: He is not going to make this easy on us.Big comeback for Scheffler? Getty ImagesScottie Scheffler was 12 shots back to begin the third round.Should he win tomorrow, it would be the second-largest 36-hole comeback to win a men's major all-time.George Duncan was 13 shots behind Abe Mitchell through 2 rounds at the 1920 Open.Big change today for McIlroy Getty ImagesRory McIlroy when missing the fairway on par-4s and par-5s this weekFirst two rounds: 7-under-par, 8 birdiesSaturday: 2-over-par, 0 birdiesScheffler flirted with history Getty ImagesAmid Scottie Scheffler’s chase for his third Masters win, the golfer flirted with another feat in the third round Saturday.Scheffler shot a 7-under 65, falling just two strokes short of the course record set by Nick Price (1986) and Greg Norman (1996) at Augusta National. The round tied tournament leader Rory McIlroy for the best round at Augusta so far this year.Scheffler had a rough second round, shooting a 2-over 74 on Friday, but bounced back to surge up the leaderboard Saturday with a blazing start. He eagled the par-5 second hole and proceeded to make par on the next four holes. The 29-year-old then finished the front nine with three straight birdies to jump into the top five and make the turn at 31.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAce gave Lowry's round a spark Getty Images Shane Lowry pulled himself into the thick of Masters contention Saturday in the most thrilling way possible: with a hole-in-one on the par-3 sixth hole, making Lowry the first golfer in Masters history to record multiple aces at the historic tournament. The hole-in-one was the first at the Masters since Stewart Cink in 2022 on the 16th hole. Lowry became the seventh golfer to ace the sixth hole in tournament history, a feat most recently accomplished by Corey Conners in 2021. Lowry’s masterful shot moved him into a tie for second place with a score of 8 under. Cantlay is a 'work in progress' Getty ImagesBefore the Masters started, I spent a little time with Hall-of-Fame caddie Joe LaCava. We talked about his old boss, Tiger Woods. We talked about our mutual interest in the New York Giants. We shook hands out in front of the clubhouse, and then it hit me that I hadn’t asked Joe a single thing about his current boss.Patrick Cantlay. A highly accomplished player with only one top-10 finish this year.“It’s coming,” LaCava said. “He’s a work in progress.”Just like your Giants, I told the caddie.And then Cantlay went ahead and shot himself right out of the Masters with an opening-round 77. He was done. Stick-a-fork-in-him cooked.Only a funny thing happened on the way to a missed Masters cut. Cantlay shot 67 on Friday to make it to the weekend, then shot 66 on Saturday to put himself in contention. He started the third round a dozen strokes off Rory McIlroy’s lead and now sits a mere five back of McIlroy and Cameron Young.“Yeah, had a rough day the first day,” Cantlay said in an understatement. “Just kind of a round that you throw out and try and get to work. I feel like I’ve done a good job of not staying patient, but not trying to get it all back at once and playing the right shot the last couple of days.”In other words, this work in progress put in the work ... and then made progress.Cantlay is an eight-time PGA Tour winner who hasn’t won since the 2022 BMW Championship. He is long overdue. Don’t be surprised if he makes an early Sunday charge.They didn’t use to call him “Patty Ice” for nothing, after all.More history against McIlroy Getty Images Rory McIlroy is the fifth Masters 54-hole leader since 2000 who shot 73 or higher in the third round. Only one of the previous four went on to win.2007: Stuart Appleby, No2014: Bubba Watson, Yes2016: Jordan Spieth, No2023: Brooks Koepka, NoMorikawa: 'I'm over the moon right now' Getty ImagesCollin Morikawa probably would have been one of the favorites this week if he had not injured his back at the Players Championship. So how does he feel after today’s 4-under 68 to get to 5 under for the tournament?💬 “I'm over the moon right now, and I know I have one more day. I have 18 more holes to keep fighting. It's not going to be easy. Each day I wake up, it's not easy to keep doing it.“But I love it, and very grateful that we get to do this.”Career round for Henley Getty ImagesGeorgia native Russell Henley had his best career Masters round with a 6-under 66 today. He had six birdies and no bogeys. 💬 “There were super calm conditions, and I just felt like I hit my irons great and gave myself a lot of looks for birdie and had some good par saves. I’m extremely pleased.”Henley will enter the final round at 6 under after recording three birdies in his final four holes.💬 “A lot of guys, it seems like they're ahead of me, and the course is gettable. ... But you know, if I keep playing the way I'm playing, I hope that I can keep moving up.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementHarman on his recovery, 67 today Getty ImagesAt one point in his round yesterday, Brian Harman was at 10 over. He will enter tomorrow’s final round at 1 under. So what changed?💬 “No different. I was frustrated that my golf tournament was pretty much over. But I played some great golf since then, you know. Just the golf tournament started a day too early for me.”The Georgia native fired a 67 today.💬 “I played some nice golf today but had a weird start. I had a nice up and down on 1 and played really nice.”McIlroy struggling with driver Getty ImagesFewest fairways hit by 54-hole leader/co-leader at the Masters since 1990:2026, Rory McIlroy: 212007, Stuart Appleby: 222009, Angel Cabrera: 24Day again playing well in Augusta Getty ImagesJason Day has plenty of experience around Augusta National, and he has had plenty of success with five top-10 finishes in his 14 starts.That is continuing this week as he is 8 under entering the final round after playing the first three in 69-71-68.Tomorrow offers another chance for his first Masters win.💬 “Tomorrow is the last day. You’ve just got to try and get yourself the opportunity on the back side. If you can get somewhere close to the lead on the back side, anything can happen. The goal is to try and cut into the lead tomorrow through nine, and if I can do that, great. Then get myself somewhere near the lead on the back side and try and give myself opportunities.”Day gave himself a much better opportunity with four straight birdies today on the second nine, starting at No. 12. 💬 “It was nice to be able to have the chances from 12 to 15. I hit a lot of good quality shots going into the greens. I also hit a lot of good drives to give myself the opportunities up near the greens on the par-5s.”Some history for Lowry Getty ImagesShane Lowry made some history today, becoming the first player ever at the Masters to have multiple career aces. And, oh yeah, he’s in the hunt to win the tournament.💬 “That's wild, isn't it? Made one a couple of weeks ago in Houston. You don't ever expect to make a hole-in-one. I just couldn't believe it. Obviously, you know, you're out there, and you're in the hunt at the Masters, and you're making a hole-in-one, it's pretty cool.“The walk down the sixth hole with everyone around 16 and the 6th was very special. I'll remember that for a while. Yeah, it was obviously amazing.”Lowry enters the final round at 9 under, two shots off the lead, after rounds of 70-69-68. He had four birdies, two bogeys, and of course, the hole-in-one.💬 “It gives you obviously a huge kind of boost. You go from 6-under to 8-under, and then all of a sudden you're only four back. It's getting real now.“I felt like I did a great job of calming myself down afterwards. … I hit a great tee shot on 7, and I was very happy and proud of that one, because it's easy to get a bit flustered in areas like that. Your adrenaline is pumping.”Some interesting notes about tomorrow Getty ImagesSome numbers to know about tomorrow:The last nine Masters winners came from the final pairing on SundayThirty of the last 35 came from the final pairing on SundayEighty-four of the 89 Masters winners were within five shots through 54 holesNinety-five percent of men's major winners in the last 100 years have been within five shots through 54 holesSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWhat happened to Reed? Getty ImagesWhat happened to Patrick Reed today? The putter let him down. The began the day in the penultimate group but shot an even-par 72 and is tied for ninth at 6-under.On Day 1 he was one of the very best putters in the field. On Friday he was still quite good. On Saturday only five men were worst.Young on chasing McIlroy Getty ImagesLike most of Rory McIlroy’s peers, Cameron Young has great respect for the defending Masters champion and said to CBS the thought of coming back from such a massive deficit from McIlroy was daunting at the beginning of the day.💬 “There certainly is no lead that’s safe out here, but at the same time, Rory loves it here, and he’s obviously playing some great golf. I don’t think anyone would be surprised if he went out here and shot 65 today, too (like he did yesterday). It’s just one of those times that, if he does open the door, you have to take advantage, and thankfully I was able to get myself a little closer here today.” Can McIlroy get it done tomorrow? Getty Images Rory McIlroy is the eighth defending Masters champion to hold the 54-hole lead or co-lead.1952, Ben Hogan: No1954, Ben Hogan: No1959, Arnold Palmer: No1966, Jack Nicklaus: Yes1983, Craig Stadler: No2002, Tiger Woods: Yes2016, Jordan Spieth: No2026, Rory McIlroy: ?Young won't be afraid Getty ImagesIf you are a very casual golf fan who only knows the big names, here is something to understand up front about Cameron Young:He will not be afraid of Rory McIlroy or any other animate or inanimate aspect of the Masters Sunday stage.A two-time winner on the PGA Tour who is hunting his first major title, Young will start the day sharing the lead with the defending champ at 11-under. McIlroy sure had his share of struggles in Saturday’s third round, surrendering what was a record 6-shot 36-hole lead at No. 12 and shooting a 1-over 73, a country mile south of the 65 turned in by Young.But let’s face it: McIlroy is already an all-time great and winner of the career Grand Slam. He is expected to return to Thursday/Friday form in the final round and reduce Young to something of a bit player in a drama that’s supposed to end with Rory joining Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, and Tiger Woods as the only Masters champs to go back-to-back.Just don’t believe that general expectation will inspire any fear in the 28-year-old father of three and recent winner of the Players Championship, the pride of Wake Forest, Sleepy Hollow Country Club in Westchester County, New York, and Fordham Prep in the Bronx.After he won the Players last month, Young said he had devoted everything about his early-season preparation to get ready for the Masters.He remembered that in his Saturday press conference here when answering a question about how much is Players victory will help him in the mano-a-mano with Rory.“That’s really what I was trying to do, was get ready to be playing late on Sunday at Augusta,” Young said. “Now I’m here with what will be a late tee time on Sunday at Augusta, and that’s the best prep I could have asked for.”McIlroy still working on driverRory McIlroy was the last man left on the driving range but left a moment ago. He told reporters after his round that he was going to go hit some balls and try to "neutralize the ball flight a bit."💬 "I think for me it's just about keeping my lower body moving. If I can just get my lower body moving through impact, then that should — that should sort of fix it."SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFinal-round tee timesHere are the tee times for tomorrow's final round (all times ET):9:06 a.m. – Aaron Rai, Charl Schwartzel9:17 a.m. – Gary Woodland, Kurt Kitayama9:28 a.m. – Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia9:39 a.m. – Si Woo Kim, Rasmus Hojgaard9:50 a.m. – Keegan Bradley, Dustin Johnson10:01 a.m. – Matt McCarty, Corey Conners10:12 a.m. – Viktor Hovland, Justin Thomas10:23 a.m. – Alex Noren, Maverick McNealy10:45 a.m. – Adam Scott, Marco Penge10:56 a.m. – Harris English, Samuel Stevens11:07 a.m. – Brian Harman, Jordan Spieth11:18 a.m. – Sungjae Im, Hideki Matsuyama11:29 a.m. – Sepp Straka, Jacob Bridgeman11:40 a.m. – Chris Gotterup, Kristoffer Reitan11:51 a.m. – Michael Brennan, Max Homa12:13 p.m. – Nick Taylor, Matt Fitzpatrick12:24 p.m. – Ludvig Aberg, Brian Campbell12:35 p.m. – Tyrrell Hatton, Tommy Fleetwood12:46 p.m. – Brooks Koepka, Wyndham Clark12:57 p.m. – Ryan Gerard, Xander Schauffele1:08 p.m. – Jake Knapp, Ben Griffin1:30 p.m. – Patrick Reed, Collin Morikawa1:41 p.m. – Patrick Cantlay, Russell Henley1:52 p.m. – Scottie Scheffler, Haotong Li2:03 p.m. – Jason Day, Justin Rose2:14 p.m. – Sam Burns, Shane Lowry2:25 p.m. – Cameron Young, Rory McIlroyBridgeman learning in Masters debut Getty Images Jacob Bridgeman has learned a lot in his Masters debut, and he was able to use some of it today in his best round of the week, After a 74 yesterday, Bridgeman rebounded today with a 69, and he will be at 2 under entering the final round.💬 “I feel like I played probably the best of the week. I hit it really solid, played a lot of really conservative shots. Me and my caddie were talking, walking off the green. I feel like we hit every number we were trying to hit today. Just kind of that's what the course gave me. If my putter would have cooperated a little bit, I think it would have been really special, but I missed a few short ones.”Young: I'm really excited for tomorrow Getty ImagesAfter his incredible 65 for a share of the lead, Cameron Young sat down with CBS in Butler Cabin to discuss his incredible turnaround this weekend.💬 “I feel like I was really ready to go for the week, and just got off to one of those starts. Everything I did was not quite right, and this place will take it to you when it’s going that way. So really just a turnaround of some really small things, and very grateful to have done that and be sitting here today.“I feel that I’ve been around the lead in major championships for a good few years now, but never here. I think I played a good round here on Sunday to finish in the top 10, but no real chance to win. So I'm just really excited to get to playing golf tomorrow.“The last few weeks, I’ve been playing some really nice golf, and just thankful to be doing some more of it here.”Reed vs. Rose Getty ImagesOn the first tee, Patrick Reed was met with mild (at best) applause. Justin Rose arrived next and was met with a loud cheer that was meant to be inspiring.Which player led the local school, Augusta State, to back-to-back NCAA championships, and which one was born in South Africa and raised in England?Reed has long been golf’s most polarizing player, so perhaps it was fitting Saturday that he was dressed in all black. Dustups over rules infractions, defamation lawsuits, a longtime estrangement from his family, the jump into and out of LIV — the noise has defined his career more than his 2018 victory at the Masters, which wasn’t exactly celebrated the way Tiger Woods’s was the following year.So it wasn’t terribly surprising that his beautiful approach into the first hole, which led to a birdie, was again greeted by an obligatory golf clap, nothing more. The response was louder for Reed’s birdie at No. 2, and almost rousing for his birdie at No. 3, which left him two strokes off the lead.On a hot Saturday, perhaps the locals were warming up to the local. Reed dropped a couple of shots over the next two holes, but he was still very much in the tournament.He had time to win over the fans, and to remind them that, in happier times, he was a Ryder Cup hero, a conqueror of Rory McIlroy, and a swaggering star worthy of the nickname “Captain America.”This isn’t about winning over America anymore.This is about winning over Augusta.Is it finally time for Rose to climb the top step? Getty ImagesThere would be few, if any, more popular winners of this year's Masters than Justin Rose.The Englishman is the perennial nearlyman at this place, with three runner-up finishes including last year's dramatic playoff defeat.But the most impressive aspect of that playoff defeat is that Rose made it to the playoff in the first place. He had 10 — yes, 10 — birdies in last year's final round as he carded a 6-under 66 to reel in Rory McIlroy.Rose started last year's final round six shots back from the lead. He will start tomorrow just three shots back.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMcIlroy still in great shape Getty ImagesRory McIlroy still has a great chance to join an elite club tomorrow. He is tied for the lead with Cameron Young at 11 under. McIlroy is trying to become the fourth player to win the Masters in consecutive years, joining Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods.💬 “There are a lot of guys in with a chance tomorrow. I'm still tied for the best score going into tomorrow, so I can't forget that, but I do know I'm going to have to be better if I want to have a chance to win.”A 'clean card' for Rose Getty ImagesJustin Rose just keeps giving himself chances to win the Masters. He is at 8 under entering the final round after shooting a 3-under 69 today.💬 “I guess there are places you just get to even before you get to the golf course. You just arrive here and take a deep breath. It's familiar faces, the same guys in the locker room. You get to know some of the members. It begins to feel comfortable. It's always special. It never gets complacent.“That's the magic that I'm comfortable here, but never complacent here. I feel like there's always something to learn, something to push for. You've always got to respect the golf course. I think we're seeing it this year.”Rose finished as the runner-up for the third time in his Masters career last year, but he’s right back in the fight. He started his tournament with rounds of 70-69 before his bogey-free round today.💬 “I felt like I could have made a couple more birdies. I’ve just got to get the putter hot really. The last couple of days, I haven't been able to quite free it up on the greens. They maybe look fast. They look really fast. A bit of hesitation in there maybe. I’ve got to get that out for tomorrow.“If you make one bogey, it really does slow your momentum. I’ll always take a clean card.”Burns put himself in strong position Getty ImagesSam Burns has a terrific chance to win his first major tomorrow after a bogey-free 4-under 68. He is one shot behind leaders Rory McIlroy and Cameron Young.💬 “I feel like I've played a really solid round. Felt like I was patient. I tried to just take what the golf course was giving me and felt like I hit a lot of quality shots and hit some good putts that I made; hit some good putts that I didn't.”Burns played with McIlroy today and didn’t get distracted by the narrative surrounding the defending champion💬 “Ultimately, I'm playing the golf course. You know, I can't control anything anyone else does. I can only control myself, and so that's kind of what the mentality we took today. Just focus on our process and go out there and compete.”Get ready for a huge final round Getty ImagesWhen we all went to bed last night, there was a worry that tomorrow might be a bit of a cake walk for Rory McIlroy. But anyone who has watched the Northern Irishman at any stage in his career knew that he might be due a wobble.And he was.His driving was poor on Thursday and Friday, despite him having a record lead last evening, and it cost him dearly today. Instead of a McIlroy procession, we have got a proper barnstorming final round in store tomorrow.If you needed a reminder, here are all the golfers within five shots of his and Cameron Young's lead:Sam Burns (-10)Shane Lowry (-9)Jason Day (-8)Justin Rose (-8)Scottie Scheffler (-7)Haotong Li (-7)Patrick Cantlay (-6)Russell Henley (-6)Patrick Reed (-6)Some serious star power there!Who were today's top performers? Today's third-round action provided plenty of drama, including shake-ups across the leaderboard. Spectators also witnessed the second and third 7-under 65 rounds of the tournament and those rounds' impact on the standings.Here are the top five performers from today:Cameron Young: 65Scottie Scheffler: 65Patrick Cantlay: 66Russell Henley: 66Brian Harman: 67Five players recorded a 68, including Sam Burns, Shane Lowry and Jason Day in the top five.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty ImagesOnly two players in the top 10 entering the final round of the Masters shot in the 70s today: Rory McIlroy (73) and Patrick Reed (72).McIlroy: 'I'll need to be better tomorrow' Getty ImagesRory McIlroy wore a long face as he walked off the 18th green, knowing that he could have put himself in a much more commanding position. But he still co-leads the tournament heading into the final round — here is what he said to Sky Sports.💬 “I knew today wasn't going to be easy. The quality of the chasing pack was very obvious and a lot of the guys played superb golf. Starting with Scottie, then Cam and everyone else. I didn't quite have it today, from the first hole making that soft bogey, I was doing my best to hang on — I scrambled well on the front nine.“I would have wanted to be in a better position tomorrow having started with a six-shot lead but I still have a great chance. I'm in the final group which is exactly where you want to be. I wish I had a bit more of a cushion.“I'm going to head to the range here to try to figure it out. I'll need to be better tomorrow.”No post-round news conference for McIlroy Getty Images Masters press center announcer: 💬 “Rory McIlroy will be invited to the interview room.”Announcer five minutes later: 💬 “Rory McIlroy will *not* be coming to the interview room.”Young's confidence continues to grow Getty Images Cameron Young matched the best round of the week with a 7-under 65 today as he chases his first major championship win.He had eight birdies and one bogey while hitting 16 of 18 greens in regulation.💬 “It's a place that I love. I've been fortunate enough to play, this is my fifth Masters, and every time I come back it's a special place to be. A Saturday 65 is not something I can complain about.”Young is trying to become the fourth player to win the Players Championship and the Masters in the same year. His first win came last year, and there is just a difference in his game since then.💬 “I think it's been a slow climb. The hardest thing to do, I think, is develop some confidence when things aren't going great. Through the middle of last year, I was able to take some positives out of some average results and out of some close calls.”Is it Cameron Young's time? Getty Images Cameron Young will receive enormous praise for the way he has played over the last two days, and boy does he deserve it!The New Yorker barely put a foot wrong all day — aside from plopping the ball into the water on 15 — and has a fantastic chance of winning his first major championship tomorrow.It is incredibly hard to believe he was four over par through his first seven holes on Thursday, and there have been only two birdies on his cards since.The New Yorker will be mightily popular winner if he gets over the line in 24 hours' time.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAnother day of Masters drama in the books! Getty Images Surely you never thought Rory McIlroy was going to run away with it?The Northern Irishman never does it easily at this place and he will make up an mouth-watering final pair alongside Cameron Young tomorrow evening.He was nowhere near his best, but he did well to limit the damage as he threatened to fall apart at Amen Corner. And he will have taken a share of the lead heading into the final round had you offered him that at the beginning of the week.Two men will ride into tomorrow 11 under and six others will start within four shots of the lead. I can't wait!McIlroy cards 1-over 73 to share 54-hole lead with Young Getty ImagesNo closing birdie for Rory McIlroy, though he came mightily close to it from 22 feet.He will hand in a card reading 73, 1 over par and enough for a share of a lead with Cameron Young. He never felt in any control of that round, but has just managed to keep his head above water and will start in the final round tomorrow.It was a very solid, if unspectacular, round from McIlroy's playing partner Sam Burns. He finished with a run of five-straight birdies on a bogey-free 4-under 68 round.He will start Sunday at the Masters one shot back from the leaders.What a final day we have in store tomorrow!Rose scores 69, Reed ends with a bogey Getty ImagesAfter a stunning start, Patrick Reed will be disappointed to end his third round with a level-par 72.He was not helped by putting his approach at the 18th into a greenside bunker with led to a bogey that put him back to mark he started the day on, 6 under par.For Justin Rose, it was a bogey-free round completed with a 15th par at the last.Lowry cards a 68 to stay in the mix He won’t get into the final pairing with Rory McIlroy. But Shane Lowry has put himself right in contention for his first green jacket, ending the day with four straight pars (starting with his save on 15) to card a 68 today.That puts him at 9 under through 54 holes. As things stand right now, he’ll be alongside Sam Burns in the second-to-last group.The highlight of course — his incredible hole-in-one on the 6th.Tommy Fleetwood, meanwhile, finishes with a 73 to tumble down the leaderboard this week. He’s now at 4 under on the weekend.McIlroy drops a shot at the 17th Getty ImagesNo sign of a stress-free par at the par-four 17th for Rory McIlroy whose whopping tee shot bailed out to the left again and settled right at the base of a particularly large pine tree.It left him a tiny window to the green and he managed to clip his approach onto that green, but no sooner it had raced on, it raced straight off the back side to leave a fairly straightforward up and down, by his ridiculous standards.Hmm. Not what quite he was looking for, but only nine or ten feet for par. And he didn't hit it, so that's a dropped shot for the defending champ.Sam Burns was safely aboard the green in two but with a few feet more than 30 for a birdie three, so he settled for par.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFour pars in a row for Reed and Rose Getty ImagesBoth Patrick Reed and Justin Rose gave themselves long birdie chances at 17, Rose from more than 50 feet and Reed from well in excees of 20.But both went agonisingly close to making them before tapping in for pars.That is four pars in a row for the both of them and Rose heads for the 18th on the brink of a bogey-free round.Li on his weekHaotong Li’s first appearance in the Masters since 2019 and just his third overall certainly has been one to remember. Li is tied for seventh at 7 under after rounds of 71-69-69. He has been battling an illness and hit two balls into the water today. He had a very animated reaction after his approach went in the water on No. 15:💬 “Just some negative thoughts between my backswing. Somehow, something clicked, I don't know. Yeah, I was very disappointed.”Clark's third round ends with consecutive bogeys Getty ImagesWhile Tyrrell Hatton wrapped up his third round with a birdie, his playing mate Wyndham Clark went out on a bitter note.On No. 18, Clark missed the green on a would-be approach shot, and his 13-foot putt a couple strokes later missed to the right by a couple feet. Clark held a lead over Hatton for most of Saturday thanks to his eagle on No. 3, but they end in the same place they started – tied with each other at 4 under.Hatton closes out with a birdie It wasn't his scorching 66 on Friday, but Tyrrell Hatton completed a solid round of golf with his second birdie of the day as the final flair.On No. 18, Hatton used a spectacular approach shot to land on the green and a 16-foot putt to wrap up his day. He ends even for the day and 4 under, tying him for 15th place.Stress-free par for McIlroy on 16 Getty ImagesThe first drama-free par for Rory McIlroy in what feels like an age.He drew his tee shot at the par-three 16th into the big part of the green, a long way from the hole — 38 feet away, in fact.
